t:
Section 3 of said Act (21 U.S.C. 452) is hereby amended to read:


“Sec. 3. 
It is hereby declared to be the policy of the Congress to provide for the inspection of poultry and poultry products and otherwise regulate the processing and distribution of such articles as hereinafter prescribed to prevent the movement or sale in interstate or foreign commerce of, or the burdening of such commerce by, poultry products which are adulterated or misbranded. It is the intent of Congress that when poultry and poultry products are condemned because of disease, the reason for condemnation in such instances shall be supported by scientific fact, information, or criteria, and such condemnation under this Act shall be achieved through uniform inspection standards and uniform applications thereof.”

fable.w: This section is a congressional declaration of policy and intent on poultry inspection and condemnation standards. The tempting reading is that the word "regulate" implies rulemaking, or that "scientific fact, information, or criteria" implies consulting outside experts. Neither holds: the section grants no rulemaking authority and sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: It is hereby declared to be the policy of the Congress to provide for the inspection of poultry and poultry products and otherwise regulate the processing and distribution of such articles as hereinafter prescribed

opus.w: This section is a statement of congressional policy and intent about poultry inspection. It does not set up any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Requiring that condemnations rest on scientific fact sets an evidence standard. It does not bring any outside party into a federal decision.
opus.s: It is the intent of Congress that when poultry and poultry products are condemned because of disease, the reason for condemnation in such instances shall be supported by scientific fact, information, or criteria, and such condemnation under this Act shall be achieved through uniform inspection standards and uniform applications thereof.
opus.b: **Tempting reading:** The phrase "supported by scientific fact, information, or criteria" sounds like outside experts might be involved, and "uniform inspection standards" sounds like rulemaking. Neither holds up. The text only says what condemnations must be based on. It never requires consulting scientists or anyone else outside the government, and it doesn't call for regulations, a comment period or a hearing.

qwen_chat.w: This section declares congressional policy regarding the standards for poultry inspection and condemnation. It requires that condemnations be based on scientific fact and uniform standards, but it does not mandate any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as experts, states, or the public) in making those decisions. The reference to 'scientific fact' is a substantive standard, not a procedural requirement for external participation.
qwen_chat.s: It is the intent of Congress that when poultry and poultry products are condemned because of disease, the reason for condemnation in such instances shall be supported by scientific fact, information, or criteria, and such condemnation under this Act shall be achieved through uniform inspection standards and uniform applications thereof.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for "scientific fact, information, or criteria" implies consultation with outside experts. However, the text does not mandate any specific process for obtaining that scientific input (e.g., an advisory committee or public comment). It merely sets a standard for the basis of condemnation decisions. There is no requirement to consult with anyone outside the federal government.
